scenes.label: Hook + setup
scenes.text: This is a piece I wrote about why most agent strategies aren't compounding. Every new initiative rebuilds the same plumbing from scratch: skills, adapters, audit, governance. After a year, instead of a platform, you have a graveyard of prototypes. The alternative is a shared substrate every initiative inherits.

scroll_sequence.to_text: Each of these initiatives is a hand-copied manuscript

scenes.label: What's in the substrate
scenes.text: So what's actually in this substrate. [BREAK:400] Four pieces. [BREAK:300] The harness keeps your code deterministic, and only calls the model inside narrow, supervised bands. So you never bet a whole workflow on the model behaving. [BREAK:500] Skills sit on top. Just markdown files, owned by one team, that any workflow can pull in. [BREAK:500] MCPs are adapters to your real outside systems. You connect once, and every agent in every workflow inherits it. [BREAK:500] And underneath, one YAML file for identity, audit, validation, and policy. Compliance ends up with one surface to look at, not one per project.

scroll_sequence.to_text: What you ought to be using instead

scenes.label: Workflow in flight
scenes.text: Here's one of those workflows in flight. [BREAK:400] Accounts payable invoice from a supplier called Globex. Two hundred and ninety five thousand pounds. [BREAK:500] The agent has worked through it, looked the supplier up, matched it against the purchase order, and got as far as it could. [BREAK:400] But the amount is over the threshold of the person who'd normally counter-sign, so it's paused, waiting on her. [BREAK:600] What you're looking at is the agent's decision, the authority rule it consulted, its reasoning, and the audit trail. All on one page. [BREAK:400] All replayed from a real run that happened against the substrate I just described.

scenes.label: Authority matrix
scenes.text: One thing worth flagging while we're here. [BREAK:400] All those approval calls. Who can sign off, at what amount, who they escalate to when they can't. [BREAK:500] That's a real matrix that exists in your organisation today. The substrate makes it machine-readable, so the agents look up the same rules your humans do. [BREAK:500] They never decide on their own. They route the work to whoever owns it, and the matched rule lands in the audit log alongside their reasoning.

scenes.label: Memory
scenes.text: This is the substrate's memory. [BREAK:400] Every run leaves a trace, organised by domain. [BREAK:300] These are real hiring cases the substrate has processed. What the agent recommended, who signed off, the signals that drove the call. [BREAK:600] When the next hiring case opens, the substrate pulls the relevant past entries into the agent's context. [BREAK:400] After enough runs, the agent acts like it's been doing this job for years. Because in aggregate, it has.

scenes.label: Constellation + knowledge graph
scenes.text: This is the whole organisation in one view. [BREAK:500] Each ring is a department. Each city inside that ring is a domain. And the rockets you can see flying between them, those aren't decorative. Each one is an actual workflow in flight, right now, against the substrate. [BREAK:700] Now watch when I flip over to the entities side. [BREAK:600] Now you can see what those workflows are actually touching. People, money, decisions, suppliers, all in one connected graph. [BREAK:500] Every workflow projects what it touches onto this graph. So the next agent that picks up a case finds the history already there. The substrate compounds.

scenes.label: Closing
scenes.text: That's the substrate. [BREAK:500] Everything you've just seen, the harness, the skills, the operator, the constellation view, all of it is built and runs the same way. Every piece is a skill the agent can read and extend. [BREAK:700] If you want to look at it yourself, the whole piece is at this URL. There's a Let's talk link at the bottom of the article that puts thirty minutes on my calendar. No slides, no pitch. [BREAK:500] Thank you for your time.
